holidays.name: International No Diet Day
holidays.description: A day to put down the calorie counter, enjoy the cake, and make peace with the body you have. It's a cheerful protest against diet culture and the idea that happiness comes in one size.
holidays.origin: British campaigner Mary Evans Young started it in 1992. She directed a group called Diet Breakers and wanted to challenge society's obsession with weight and dieting. It began in the UK and spread to other countries.
holidays.funFact: The day's symbol is a light blue ribbon. Its early organizers also encouraged people to ceremonially burn or toss out their bathroom scales.

holidays.name: National No Pants Day
holidays.description: An unofficial observance that invites you to lose the trousers for a day. You can stay home in comfort or swap in a breezy skirt or dress. It's a day to celebrate freedom, comfort, and the joy of loungewear.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial, playful observance of unclear origin. It has spread through quirky-holiday calendars and social media as an excuse to be as comfortable as possible.
holidays.funFact: It's often confused with the Annual No Pants Subway Ride, which started in 2002 with a handful of people in New York City. That event is held in January, not on May 6.
